title: Per-tenant adaptive SLO allocation and phased rollout policy for mixed-latency workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD: Define a per-tenant SLO allocation mechanism and a phased rollout policy that supports mixed-latency workloads (interactive chat + embeddings). This ticket clarifies scope and acceptance criteria for: 1) how to map tenant-priority tiers to dynamic error budgets and p99/p95 latency envelopes, 2) rollout gates that combine burn-rate, region health, and per-tenant isolation signals, and 3) contract tests and automated checks required before a tenant is bumped to a higher performance tier. Scope changes since initial RFC: we are narrowing immediate rollout to hosted-api customers (no Dedicated or Private for phase 1) and deferring token-cost accounting into a follow-up. This ticket coordinates product decisions, sig-term trade-offs, engineering work on contract tests, and dashboards required by SRE and Customer Success.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant SLO mapping table published in PRD (tiers: free, standard, enterprise) with explicit p50/p95/p99 latency targets and availability goals for each API surface (chat, generate, embeddings)

Automated contract test suite (GitHub Actions) that validates: synthetic traffic at target QPS achieves expected latency envelope and that fallback routing triggers under simulated capacity constraint
Rollout policy implemented as config in runtime-ops repo with gates: burn-rate threshold, regional error spikes, per-tenant isolation metric (KV cache miss ratio), and manual approval flag
Console dashboard tile that shows per-tenant rolling error budget consumption (1h, 6h, 24h) and a link-to-runbook for high-burn incidents
Canary run plan that progresses a cohort of 5 enterprise tenants -> 25 tenants -> global with automated rollback if aggregated burn rate exceeds 2x baseline for 30m
A /contract-tests endpoint returns pass/fail and historical results; PR must include a passing run in CI for the merge to be approved
Customer-facing SLA language (SLA PDF and billing contract clauses) drafted and reviewed by legal for enterprise tier
